title: SDLC Task Implementation v1
description: The task-specific payload for implementing a bounded change and recording implementation-owned verification evidence. Intent describes expected change surfaces, reason for change, authoritative inputs, objectives, owned paths, exclusions, and planned steps. Result records semantic changes, concrete test implementations, grouped verification executions, and limitations. Requirement, invariant, and acceptance-criterion coverage belongs to the governing test strategy and is not duplicated here.
$comment: The common https://schemas.handschuh.dev/sdlc/task-envelope/v1 owns task identity, processing state, dependencies, routing, repository context, and the common task wrapper. Host validation must resolve relationships that JSON Schema cannot establish: inputRefs resolve to intent.inputs; objectiveRefs resolve to intent.objectives; change types are declared by intent.changeTypes; required inputs are available; a selected strategy input identifies a completed https://schemas.handschuh.dev/sdlc/task-test-strategy/v1 result; objective testCaseRefs resolve to strategy-defined or implementation-owned cases; testImplementations point to actual repository test artifacts; required strategy cases have successful executions before verification may be passed; changed paths remain inside ownedPaths; and verification does not claim evidence beyond the canonical https://schemas.handschuh.dev/sdlc/evidence/v1 tiers and strategy limitations. This payload intentionally does not repeat requirement, invariant, acceptance-criterion, or strategy coverage mappings.

intent.description: The prospective implementation contract and authoritative source boundary.

examples.summary: Implement validation before persistence according to the completed test strategy.

result.description: The retrospective implementation output and actual verification evidence.

ChangeType.description: A category of meaningful implementation output. production-code is runtime or library code; test-code is automated test code or test infrastructure; configuration is application, runtime, repository, or tool configuration; schema is a machine-readable contract; migration transforms persisted state; infrastructure covers deployment, cloud, networking, CI/CD, container, or infrastructure-as-code material; dependency records an intentional dependency change; documentation is maintained explanatory or operational content; generated-artifact is an intentionally persisted generated output.

ChangeIntent.description: The primary reason for performing the implementation. feature introduces or extends behavior; bugfix corrects behavior; refactor changes internal structure without intended observable change; performance improves resource use or responsiveness; security strengthens a security boundary; compatibility preserves interoperability; maintenance covers other implementation upkeep.

InputKind.description: The semantic kind of an authoritative implementation input. testStrategy identifies a completed strategy result governing verification; task identifies another task or task result; design identifies a design result or model; the remaining values identify the corresponding source category.

ImplementationResultStatus.description: The observed implementation outcome, independent of verification. implemented means intended work was completed; partially-implemented means a meaningful subset was completed; blocked means an unresolved dependency or external condition prevented progress; failed means the attempt did not produce a viable implementation.

VerificationStatus.description: The aggregate observed verification result. passed means applicable required executions succeeded; failed means a required execution failed; partial means evidence exists but the required set is incomplete; blocked means execution could not complete; not-run means no execution was performed.

TestType.description: The highest evidence type actually exercised by one grouped verification execution. static is deterministic file or schema inspection; unit isolates a small unit; component exercises a bounded component; cli-audit checks a command boundary; integration exercises multiple real components; manual is human-performed; inspection is static examination; provider uses an external provider; operational exercises a deployed or running system.

ExecutionStatus.description: The observed outcome of one grouped verification execution. passed means referenced cases met their pass criteria; failed means one or more did not; blocked means no observable result was reached; inconclusive means evidence was insufficient to classify the cases.
